subject: Dedicated capacity sizing & pricing — follow-up
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Li <evan@brightlayer.com>, Priya Shah <priya@brightlayer.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing & pricing — follow-up

Hi Evan / Priya — great talking earlier today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps. I pasted the most important numbers below and flagged the open questions.

Highlights from the call:
- Target workload: user-facing chat + light batch reranking for analytics pipelines.
- Estimated steady-state volume: ~750M tokens / month (current baseline + 9–12 month growth plan).
- Peak profile: short spikes up to ~120–150 concurrent requests; average response ~250–350 tokens.
- Desired unit-economics target: BrightLayer aiming for an effective cost in the range of $30–$45 per 1M tokens (target = $35 / 1M tokens).
- Compliance: SOC 2 and retention controls required (you asked for evidence).

Dedicated capacity qualification items (what we discussed and what I need to confirm):
1) GPU family preference — you mentioned A100 familiarity, but asked about H100 tradeoffs (latency vs cost). Please confirm if you have a strict prohibition for any GPU type.
2) Reserved capacity size — rough target from call: 6–10 GPUs depending on SKU (we'll propose two scenarios).
3) Throughput SLOs — is P99 latency target <= 250 ms per token generation step acceptable, or do you need lower?
4) Budget cadence — is the budget review monthly or annual commit (you mentioned annual reserved preferred if unit economics work).

What I will send next (by EOD tomorrow unless you ask otherwise):
- Two SKU scenarios (A100 vs H100) with monthly reserved pricing, expected throughput, and derived $/1M tokens.
- A one-page pilot proposal (30 day, 50% capacity pilot option) and a short checklist of SOC 2 artifacts.

Attachments referenced on the call: we asked you to send the traffic profile spreadsheet — please attach when you can (traffic_profile_q1.xlsx recommended).

Next steps / asks from BrightLayer:
- Please send the traffic_profile_q1.xlsx or a CSV export with: daily tokens, median/95/99 latency requirements, and an estimated monthly growth rate.
- Confirm whether A100-only is a hard requirement or if we can include an H100 scenario.

Thanks — I CC'd Marissa (pricing) and Aditya (solutions architecture) so we can turn this into a formal estimate quickly.

Best,
Jonas
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-one-pager.pdf (summary)]

From: Evan Li <evan@brightlayer.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@brightlayer.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 10:09:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing & pricing — follow-up

Thanks Jonas — good summary. A few clarifications: 

- GPU constraint: we're not prescriptive but our infra team has validated on A100 so that's our baseline preference. We'll consider H100 only if you can show a clear cost / latency win.
- Attached is the traffic_profile_q1.xlsx export (daily tokens + 95/99 latency percentiles). Let me know if you need a different format.
- Budget cadence: our finance team prefers annual commitments if we can hit the $/1M token targets.

Two quick asks from our side before you prepare scenarios: 
1) Can you provide both a conservative (6x A100) and aggressive (10x A100) reserved layout with expected sustained tokens/month and peak throughput?
2) Show the effective $/1M tokens broken down into: reserved cost amortized + estimated variable infra/egress, and any usage-based platform fees.

We'd also like a short note on what fallback routing would look like if we hit sustained spikes beyond reserved capacity (e.g., cross-region burst or hosted fallback).

--
Evan Li
VP Product, BrightLayer Analytics
[Attachment: traffic_profile_q1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 72KB)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Li <evan@brightlayer.com>, Priya Shah <priya@brightlayer.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing & pricing — follow-up

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the spreadsheet, Evan — that helps a lot. Attached is an initial estimate PDF with two scenarios and the math behind the effective $/1M tokens. High-level summary below.

Scenario A — Baseline (A100-80GB, 6 GPUs reserved)
- Reserved pool: 6 x A100-80GB
- Estimated sustained capacity: ~450–600M tokens / month at target latency SLOs (headroom for modest bursts)
- Monthly reserved cost (incl. Redwood Dedicated platform fee): $12,500 / month
- Estimated variable infra/egress & ops: ~$2,400 / month (profile-dependent)
- Effective cost (reserved + variable) = ~$14,900 / month -> equivalent = ~$33 / 1M tokens (assuming 450M tokens).

Scenario B — Scale (A100-80GB, 10 GPUs reserved)
- Reserved pool: 10 x A100-80GB
- Estimated sustained capacity: ~750–1,100M tokens / month
- Monthly reserved cost (incl. Redwood Dedicated platform fee): $19,000 / month
- Estimated variable infra/egress & ops: ~$3,800 / month
- Effective cost (reserved + variable) = ~$22,800 / month -> equivalent = ~$30 / 1M tokens (assuming 750M tokens).

H100 alternative (four H100-80GB nodes) — short note
- H100 provides better throughput per card for some model families, which can reduce the number of GPUs required but typically has higher per-GPU hourly cost. For BrightLayer's profile I estimate a 15–25% reduction in effective $/1M tokens if your model is H100-optimizable; we will validate with a quick perf test if you'd like to pursue.

Other notes:
- Pilot option: 30-day pilot at 50% of the Scenario B pool (5 GPUs) — this lets us validate token mix and latency at scale; pilot pricing would be a pro-rated reserved fee + reduced platform onboarding credit.
- Fallbacks: Redwood can route overflow to a hosted capacity pool (managed) or cross-region burst. We include automatic fallbacks as a policy; SLA for fallback depends on priority tier.
- Compliance: attaching the SOC 2 artifact checklist in the PDF. We'll share SOC 2 report via a secure link once NDA is in place.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm which scenario (Baseline vs Scale vs H100 test) you want formalized into an SOW.
- If you want the pilot, we can prepare a short SOW and a 30-day runbook.
- Marissa will prepare a formal estimate doc and send a DocuSign link if you want to lock an annual commit.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sku-estimate.pdf (contains detailed line-item math and assumptions).

Thanks — I left the detailed math in the PDF so you and finance can validate assumptions quickly.

Jonas
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-dedicated-sku-estimate.pdf (pdf, 120KB)]

From: Evan Li <evan@brightlayer.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@brightlayer.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing & pricing — follow-up

Jonas — this is exactly what we needed. Quick answers: 
- We'll aim for the Scale scenario (10x A100) but would like to run a 30-day pilot first at 50% (5x A100) as you suggested.
- Finance is happy to look at an annual commit if the pilot validates the $/1M tokens in your estimate.
- Please share SOC 2 report link and a concise SOW for the pilot (we prefer a one-page SOW + runbook).

Also: can Marissa outline the invoicing cadence and any early-termination rules for the pilot? We'll need that for procurement.

Thanks — cc'ing Priya who will own the pilot onboarding.

Best,
Evan
VP Product, BrightLayer Analytics
